utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Russo, I see that you are apparently ready to call your next witness, Mr. Berikoff. Good morning, sir. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing about the truth. The text it now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May invite you to make that solemn declaration, but could I ask you to stand first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Berikoff. Mr. Russo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you would, please, state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Philip Roy Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, do you recall giving four statements to the ICTY, the first dated 24 August 1996, the second on 21 May 1997, the third between 26 and 27 May 1997, and the fourth and final dated 11 December 2007?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if I could have the assistance of the court usher, I would like to hand hard copies to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Berikoff, did you have a chance to review all four of those statements prior to coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I have. We did proofing sessions with you the majority of last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And in reviewing those statements, can you tell the Court whether they accurately reflect what you told investigators at the time those statements were taken?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: All four statements reflect accurately what I had to say in the statements, with the exception of the corrections that we made during the proofing sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to take you through those corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And we can just do this briefly with the indulgence of the court and counsel. Your Honour, I will simply lead Mr. Berikoff through those.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: First, as a general matter, Mr. Berikoff, in your statements, you sometimes use the terms "special police HV," "special police," and "Croatian special police." Can you clarify for the Court whether these terms are intended to refer to the same group of individuals.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, they are. It was my assumption when I was there that all three worked together because I had seen the various types of military police or special police working together. Sometimes, they would be wearing grey coveralls and sometimes camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you distinguish special police from regular HV troops?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: The special police, when they were conducting special police operations, in my opinion were those wearing grey coveralls. The ones doing normal military police duties were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And can I take it, then, that then when you refer in your statements and attachments to special police, you are referring to individuals wearing grey coveralls?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And also, in particular, in your statements and in the attachments to them, you attributed the burning and looting that you witnessed in Kistanje on 9 August 1995 to both the HV and the special police. I believe, however, that you clarified that did you not actually witness any special police members; that is, those wearing grey coveralls in the town of Kistanje on 9 August 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I just ask you to please briefly pause after my question, and I will pause after your answers. And I would like to take you through some specific references that you made to the special police for corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit D284 [Realtime transcript read in error "D248"], which is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Berikoff, this is your third statement which in your witness binder appears at tab 3. And if we could go to page 19, lines 36 through 38; in the B/C/S version, there appears at page 14, lines 26 through 29. And there, Mr. Berikoff, I believe you make a reference to the special police, when, in fact, I believe you indicated that that particular incident was the civilian police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could then move you to the following page, page 20, and that would be line 6 to 8; and in the B/C/S, that is at page 14. That would be lines 34 through 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honours, my understanding from the registrar is that apparently the B/C/S translation has not been uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On your own list, I see that it says, "B/C/S translation on progress." That's the list you filed with the -- I don't know whether it's ready. I don't know whether it is uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Apparently, it has not been uploaded yet at this point, Your Honour; however, we will ensure that that happens as soon as possible. I do have the B/C/S page numbers for the court registrar that can I provide so that we can correct the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it, then, that the translation is ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It is ready, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is ready, so if you would please take care that it is uploaded. Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Pardon me, counsel. Just by way of correction, on line 5, I think, we were talking about this document as 248. If you look at the transcript, Judge, I think it is 284.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On your list, it appears as 284.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It is it 284, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just didn't know if it was. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Berikoff. I believe we were at pages 20, lines 6 through 8. And, again, you make a reference to the special police; and, again, I believe that you had indicated that that was actually the civilian police on that occasion as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: What occasion are we looking at now? Is this still the Kistanje area, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It is, on page 20.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That is correct, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Actually, I apologise. But the page 20 line 6 to 8 is a reference to in the immediate days after Operation Storm, where you indicate that special police were directing traffic while soldiers loaded vehicles. I believe you indicated during the proofing session, that it was civilian police directing traffic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: As I explained to you last week and to the Defence yesterday that spoke to me, it was a combination of both. There was looting going on throughout the sector. However, in particular, between the road of Knin to Drnis, it was very systematic where there were a number of trucks that were lined up. There was a police -- civilian-type police standing outside on the road with a checklist, marking off that residence that the looting had taken place and that the material was put on the truck. There would also be houses that were marked with Croatian markings so as not to touch that house, and then they would go on to the next one. So it was a combination of both systematic and not systematic, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that answer. However, I wanted to simply clear up which police you were referring to directing traffic on that road. Your statement at page 20 indicates that it's special police; however, I believe you indicated --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I indicated that it was civilian police, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could move to page 24, lines 4 through 7. And here, again, are references to the incident in Kistanje on 9 August 1995. And on line 4 through 7, you indicate there that Croat soldiers and special police in coveralls were in the town. However, I believe, as you already indicated, you did not actually see special police in Kistanje on 9 August 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And also appearing further down that page, at lines 14 through 17, it makes a similar reference to special police in Kistanje; as well as at line 32, it makes a reference to special police in Kistanje. And can you simply confirm that all of those entries are incorrect in so far as they identify special police actually being in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You move to your second statement, and that is, I believe, tab 2 in your witness binder. Your second statement, for the registrar, 65 ter 3426.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we can move to page 3, paragraph 2, subparagraph O; and in the B/C/S, this appears at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And in there, Mr. Berikoff, in paragraph 2-O, you indicate that on 8 August, Croatian soldiers and special police were looting along the road between Knin and Drnis. And, again, I'd like you to correct whether it was actually civilian police rather than special police?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That's correct. It was civilian police that were checking off the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go to page 4 in that statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, have I well understood that here "special police" is replaced by "civilian police," where at the earlier instances it was just striking "special police."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Are we talking when -- pardon me, Judge. By clarification, are we talk back in 284 when counsel was striking the "special police"? I think that he was including and saying it was civilian police, when we were back on 284.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: There were two references in 284 replacing "special police" with "civilian police," and then the references to Kistanje in particular were striking "special police."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: In your second statement, Mr. Berikoff, at page 4, paragraph 2-Q, and the reference is the same in the B/C/S, you indicate that on 10 August 1995, on the road between Knin and Drnis, that looting by HV soldiers continued unabated, while special police looked on or directed traffic. I believe you had also corrected that in that instance again, it was actually civilian police and not special police directing the traffic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move back to your third statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is, again, D284.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could go to --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: What tab is that, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's tab 3 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: So D284, page 14, lines 27 through 28; and the B/C/S, this appears, for the record, at page 10, lines 46 through 48. And there, Mr. Berikoff, you give your opinion that the hospital was directly targeted during the artillery attack. However, I believe, during the proofing session, you indicated that you had changed your opinion regarding that; and, in fact, you do not believe that the hospital was actually a target of the artillery attack. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Staying with that statement, if we could move to page 21 -- 21, at lines 32 to 33; in the B/C/S, this would appear at page 15, line 45. And there, Mr. Berikoff, you indicate that you met with Major Juric on 8 August in the headquarters. However, I believe that you indicated that that date itself is not correct, and that the date that you actually met with Major Juric was the morning of 7 August?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now with the corrections we have just made, Mr. Berikoff, can you tell court whether all four of your statements taken together are true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you were questioned here today regarding the matters contained in those statements, would your answers be the same given the corrections that we've just recorded?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: At this time, Mr. President, Your Honours, I would move for the admission of the 24 August 1996 statement, which is 65 ter 5389.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P739, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I would also move admission of statement dated 21 May 1997, which is 65 ter 3426.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P740, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. The exhibit, MFI'd as D84 [sic], is the statement 26 to 27 May 1997. At this point, I would simply --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel, it is 284.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies. I thought I said 284, but apparently I can't seem to get that number correct. It's 284. I believe that would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, it slips out of my mind why it was MFI'd at that time. Was there any intention to tender it, and were we just to wait until the witness would have appeared and would have given his attestations?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think the latter explanation was a reservation by the parties until Mr. Berikoff came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, then, since you brought up the document first, would you like to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we don't have to assign another number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Actually, if I may Judge, I want to be tad gracious about this. It was actually my colleague, Mr. Mikulicic, that tendered it, so I guess I should offer the floor to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we would like to have that particular number that was MFI'D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we move to the next one, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Finally, the statement dated 11 December 2007, which is 65 ter 5391.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P741, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Now, as far as the P numbers are concerned, from the written submissions I take it that there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P739, P740, and P741 are admitted into evidence. Now, Mr. Mikulicic, Mr. Russo did part of the job seeking the attestations, you tender the documents. I take it no objections, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D284 [Realtime transcript read in error "D248"] is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With your permission, I would now like to read a brief summary of the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness knows the purpose of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am sorry to interrupt. For the purposes of correction, it is, again, "D248" in the transcript, instead of "D284."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Until it is Tuesday, we'll be able to do it correctly, Mr. Mikulicic. Thank you. Mr. Russo, let's try to avoid to refer to that number. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Philip Berikoff was the Military Information Officer in Sector South from 17 July until 5 September 1995. Prior to Operation Storm, he travelled extensively throughout Sector South collecting information on the military situation. He was present in Knin during the artillery attacks on 4 and 5 August 1995, made several missions into Knin during the shelling to rescue civilian employees and to offer assistance to the hospital, and also observed the shelling of Knin from the UN HQ compound. After Operation Storm, he managed to leave the UN HQ compound during the HV blockade and gain access to many areas in Sector South where he observed many villages on fire and also witnessed HV soldiers, special police, and civilian police engaged in looting or acts of destruction. In particular, he particularly witnessed the destruction of towns of Kistanje, Cetina, and Donji Lapac by Croatian forces. He authored several reports describing the level of destruction he witnessed in the towns and villages all over Sector South. That concludes my summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Russo. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, I would like to deal first with the attachments to your statements as well as your other exhibits, and then I will move on to ask you a few specific questions. So if you could please refer to your first statement, and that is P739. And if we could go to page 4 --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: What tab is that, please, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It's the first tab in your binder.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Again, page 4; and in the B/C/S, this appears at page 3. And there you reference a document which is attached to that statement and marked "A."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could have now 65 ter 1829, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, is the document on the screen the document which is referred to as "A" in your first statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you personally prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what the circumstances were which prompted you to do this?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: On the 22nd of November, while I was in -- after I left Knin in early September, I went on to Sarajevo to UNPROFOR Headquarters Forward as the G2 operations officer. While I was there, I got a request from UNCRO to prepare a report with regard to all of the damage that I had witnessed during my time in Sector South. I did this based on my various trips that I took while I was in Sector South. The information was based from previous reports that I had done as well as a daily journal that I kept during my whole time in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And there's a few entries that I would like to clarify. Paragraph 2-A, states: "At least 100 houses were probably destroyed during the actual offensive, 4 to 5 August 1995." Mr. Berikoff, does this number reflect the number of houses that you personally observed?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I had the opportunity shortly after the offensive to go into the town of Knin and see a number of houses that were damaged extensively. Some were damaged beyond repair. Therefore, that's why I say they were destroyed and that was immediately after. There was further destruction later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you use the term "at least 100 houses," can you give the Court some idea of approximately how many more houses you believe were damaged during the actually offensive?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: There was substantial damage to a number of other houses that I did not include in my report because I didn't -- they were still inhabitable, so I didn't include it in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving to paragraph 2-E. This paragraph discusses damage between Knin and Kistanje as well as the damage to Kistanje itself. You stated in that paragraph : "Croatian (HV special police) were likely responsible for the majority of the destruction." Can you clarify whether the destruction which you attribute in this sentence to the special police is the destruction between Knin and Kistanje or the destruction of Kistanje itself?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I would say the -- from my recollection, I would say it is the destruction in Kistanje itself and the immediate vicinity of Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And we had discussed earlier that you didn't actually see special police in Kistanje. Nevertheless, can you explain to the Court why you believe the special police had some involvement with the activity in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: It was my opinion and still is today that the special police were involved in some of the operations around the area of Kistanje, because on numerous occasions, I had met personally with Major Ivan Juric who was a military police. However, on numerous occasions when I did run into him, he was also wearing the grey coveralls of the special police. It was, therefore, my assumption that Major Juric controlled a number of the various military police and special police forces; and, in fact, by him wearing grey coveralls in that area, I assumed that there must have been special police in the area as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And to clarify, did you run into Major Juric on the day that you had also been in Kistanje on the 9th of August?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir. I ran into Major Juric in the area of Macure, which is just north of Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what he was wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Major Juric was driving in a black SUV vehicle, and he was wearing grey coveralls, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now move to paragraph 2-F -- I'm sorry, I apologise. Let's move to 2-H. And in paragraph 2-H, you discuss the damage to Oklaj, and you state: "An ARSK unit was garrisoned in the village." I'd like you to please clarify, if you can, when the ARSK unit was garrisoned in that village?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Prior -- prior to the offensive, I had --or I was tasked to a helicopter recce, along the Zone of Separation that ran between the Croat side and the Serb side. When the helicopter picked us up -- myself up at Knin, we were en route to pick up two Canadian officers in Rastovic. On the way to pick up the officers, approximately eight minutes into the flight, we were fired upon by the ARSK from the vicinity of Oklaj. They had fired one missile at us, the helicopter pilot was able to go down to ground level, and an another missile was fired at us. We returned back to the compound. I put in a protest to General Forand. General Forand further put in a protest to the ARSK. About an hour later, a colonel from the ARSK came and apologised for the incident. While we were flying over Oklaj, there were a number of ARSK vehicles, and, therefore, I assumed it was a stronghold or a garrison of ARSK soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And you just mentioned that you believed it was a stronghold. Is that why, in paragraph 2-H, you also indicate that you believe the whole village of Oklaj was or could have been a military target?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I do. There were also occasions when I drove through the town of Oklaj and observed numerous ARSK soldiers prior to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving to the following paragraph, 2-I, where you discuss damage in the village of Razvode, and you state: "Many homes were left untouched, suggesting that they were Croatian dwellings." Can you please explain to the Court why you say that the fact that they were not touched suggests that they were Croatian dwellings?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Throughout the sector and in particular in the village of Razvode, there were markings on the house, denoting the fact that, in fact, it was a Croatian residence. Therefore, that residence was left alone. The Serb residences were destroyed or damaged to an extent that made them uninhabitable.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move now, please, to paragraph 2-L, in which you discuss damage to the town of Donji Lapac, and there you state: "Much of the destruction was caused by HV special police troops." Can you tell the Court whether in Donji Lapac, you actually saw special police troops?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I went up to Donji Lapac a number of times, in particular, immediately after the offensive on Knin. There were still ongoing fighting throughout the rest of the sector because no offensive stops immediately on -- on whatever, at 1210 on the 5th of August. So there was fighting throughout the rest of the sector. When I got up to Donji Lapac, we ran into a number of HV soldier plus a number of soldiers that were dressed in grey coveralls.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what, if anything, the HV soldiers and the individuals in grey coveralls were doing in the town of Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: As I indicated just a couple of seconds ago, there was still ongoing fights so there was a lot of small-arm fire going on. However, they were also going into the houses doing whatever activity they were doing in the house. However, upon exit of the house and before the went into the next one, the house would -- would be ablaze, and it became obvious that there was destruction going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: When you say that there was fighting going on, did you see actual combat between ARSK soldiers and Croatian forces within the town of Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Not -- not right within the town itself. However, there were sounds throughout the town of small-arms fire; and, as I indicated earlier, the offensive had not stopped. It had stopped in Knin but not in areas -- other areas of the sector. So, in fact, there was still combat operations going on throughout the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move to paragraph 2-N, where you discuss damage to the village of Cetina, and there you sate: "The destruction was caused after the offensive by both the occupying HV soldiers and the Croatian special police." And can you tell the Court whether you actually sow the special police troops causing destruction in Cetina.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In addition to the HV and the special police, there was also a group of, I guess, rag-tag soldiers or possibly those that are belong to a war lord. They were also conducting looting operations or clean-up operations in the town of Cetina as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: At this time, Mr. President, I would move for the admission of 65 ter 1829.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P742, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against P742?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P742 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And moving back to your first statement, Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I don't believe we need to pull this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The first statement at pages -- between pages 4 and 5, you reference a document attached to that statement marked "B."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 450.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, is the document on the screen the document which you identify as document "B" in your first statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you please tell the Court what the circumstances were while you prepared it?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I was tasked by Major Dussault to prepare a report based on my activities during the time of the immediate aftermath of the offensive. The purpose of the document was that I was being nominated for an award, and I had to annotate those activities that I had done.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I just have one clarification for this document. At paragraph 2-B, you discussed the removal of bodies of several ARSK soldiers and civilians who were killed in a mortar blast at the intersection outside of the UN HQ compound on the morning of 5 August. And in paragraph 2-B, you indicate that the first time you went out to check these bodies you came under mortar fire and were forced to take cover in a drainage ditch. I would like to you clarify whether or not it's correct that you came under mortar fire the first time you went out there?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I do not believe we came under mortar fire the first time. The reason we went out to the intersection was because the intersection had come under mortar fire, and that is how the six people at the intersection were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you go out to that intersection for a second time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I was tasked to go out the second time in order to bag -- put the bodies in body-bags and move them off the road. There was fear of decomposition of the bodies and causing disease in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when you went to bag these bodies the second time you went out, did you come under mortar fire at that time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, we did. A mortar round went off and came within about 25 metres of our area as we were bagging the bodies. We were forced to go into a ditch alongside the road. That was the only round that hit. Once we decided that there was no more activity, we continued on with our task.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would move to admit 65 ter 450.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P743, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P743 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Referring back to your first statement, Mr. Berikoff, at page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, again, I don't believe there is any reason to pull this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You reference a document attached to first statement marked "D".

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could 65 ter 1702. And, Your Honour, I will -- I can explain to the Court why I'm not pulling up the document referenced "C" in that statement, which is a journal. There is a second journal which was submitted with the following statement which encompasses that earlier journal, and I will address that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: So, document 65 ter 1072, Mr. Berikoff, can you take a look at that and tell us whether the document on the screen is the document you referred to as document "D" in your first statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you prepare this particular document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: No, I did not. I gave bits and pieces of information. Captain Rob Williams is the gentleman that prepared the document itself, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And have had you a chance to look through the document for information that you actually provided?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And is the information which you provided actually reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And there are a few entries which I would like to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we go it page 2 of the document, this is it the entry for 4 August, 1010 Bravo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And there you indicate that you were travelling to the hospital with the SMEDLO. First, can you tell the Court what SMEDLO stands for?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: SMEDLO was the Senior Medical Officer in the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Other references to this particular trip in your statements indicate that that trip actually occurred at 1300 hours; however, this document indicates that it occurred at about 10.00 in the morning. Can you clarify for the Court whether this trip took place at 10.00 in the morning or at about 1.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, I'm uncertain of the exact timings, but I am certain of the sequence of events that took place during that day, sir. I believe it was either late, late morning or early afternoon when, in fact, we went to the hospital the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And, again, if we can move to page 3 of this document, and look at the entry for 4 August at 1300 Bravo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And there it indicates that you travelled into Knin for General Forand's press conference. And, again, other references for this particular trip in your statements indicate that it occurred at 1500 hours. And can you clarify, if you're able to, whether the trip with General Forand took place at 1.00 p.m. or at 3.00 p.m. on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: It's the same -- same answer as I previously gave. I'm certain of the sequence of events; the timings, I'm unconcern. However, I do know that we did go to the meeting in the afternoon. Another meeting was scheduled for later on that evening at 1800 hours; however, the ARSK people did not show up for the meeting, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you indicated that you're uncertain of the times, but you are certain of the sequence, can I take that to mean that you recall the trip with the SMEDLO occurring previous to the trip with General Forand?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we can move to page 4 of the document, at the entry for 5 August, 05, 0930 Bravo. There are actually two entries for that time; however, I would like to focus on the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And there it indicates that a scared ARSK soldier came to the gate of the UNHCR compound and that he was turned away? First of all, can you tell the Court whether you were the one who turned him away.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes. I was the one who turned him away. He came to the gate along with a number of other refugees; but because he was in uniform, he was carrying a weapon, we were ordered by our senior management that we were not allowed to let combatants into the compound, so I turned him away at that time, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And was this soldier that you turned away one of the soldiers killed in the mortar blast at the intersection?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document that we looked at earlier, document 743, indicated that the mortar blast occurred at that intersection at approximately 8.30; however the second entry in this particular document indicates that that blast occurred at 9.30 where you were going out to bag the bodies. Can you clarify for the Court whether the time in this document, the second entry for 05, 9.30, is incorrect or what you recall about the timing of those incidents?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: The mortar round -- the impact of the round was approximately between 8.30 and 9.00. We were tasked to go out, and it was approximately 9.30 when I went to the intersection to bag the bodies. The bodies had laid there for a period of time following the immediate mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And looking at the second entry for 9.30 Bravo, it indicates that of the six dead bodies at the intersection, where the mortar blast occurred, four were civilians and two were ARSK soldiers. However, I believe your other references indicate that it was the other way around; four soldiers and two civilians. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That's correct. It was, in fact, four soldiers and two civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And that same entry also indicates that only five of the six died from the mortar blast and one had died from a previous gunshot wound. Can you shed any light on that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: There was an elderly gentleman with a woman on a wagon. He was already dead; whether he was dead from approximate bullet shot or not, I'm not sure. One of the other soldiers I know was shot previously from a bullet shot. So, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And with those corrections, Mr. President, I believe I would like to admit this exhibit, which is 65 ter 1702.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P744, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P744 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Again, your first statement at page 5, Mr. Berikoff, references a document marked "E."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 1832.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, do you recognise the document on your screen as the document referred to as document "E" in your first statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you please explain to the Court the basis for the hierarchy that you have laid out in this chart.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: The basis for the chart or the hierarchy is on information that I had gathered either through my own investigations right within the sector or from information I had received from UNCRO. Immediately after the offensive, the first group that came in was the 7th Guards Brigade. They were relieved by the Tigers. But running into Major Juric on numerous occasions, I put him as the head of the military/special police. In this one, I have him as special police. However, on the ones that I have, all of the local police are under his jurisdiction and then the mop-up police or the special police as well. So it was based through -- the information was based on multiple sources as well as my overall assessment at the time following the offensive, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you clarify for the Court whether the line you have drawn directly above Major Juric's name, and it appears below the military structure which is underneath General Cermak, can you clarify whether that is intended to indicate your belief that Major Juric was subordinate to General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: The military police in virtually every military organisation - and I'm sure the Croatians is the same - runs a parallel chain of command. One, they answer to higher, and, secondly they answer to their immediate chain of command or their immediate operational commander. In this case, I had them answering to General Cermak following his, I guess, appointment as the head of the sector or the garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to admit 65 ter 1832.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P745, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P745 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Russo, I'm afraid that I did not fully understand the last answer. Could you try to elicit some more details from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, you've indicated your belief in this parallel chain of command between military police and regular forces. Do I understand that chart to mean that you placed Major Juric as -- within and beneath General Cermak in a reporting chain of command?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did, in the sense of General Cermak being the operational commander in -- in that immediate area. I am aware, as I said, that military police or special police also have a parallel chain of command which goes up to their own organisation, be it in Zagreb or Split or whether they are other organisation was. So at the same time that they're reporting to their immediate operational commander, they're also reporting the information to a higher authority, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you add names to that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- parallel structure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not, Your Honour. I am not able to, as I just arrived in country a few weeks prior to. So, no, I am not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Berikoff, if could you also tell the Court whether you have any specific information or specific facts to indicate whether Major Juric was, in fact, reporting to General Cermak.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I don't have any immediate information on that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And can I take it, then, that the understanding which you have reflected in this chart is based upon your experience with other military organisations and that you assumed that this is the way it worked. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is. In addition, prior to me coming to the former Yugoslavia -- or being destroyed to the former Yugoslavia, I also worked as a senior intelligence officer on the Yugoslav crisis cell at nationality defence headquarters, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move now back to your first statement, and at page 3 you --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Is the Court satisfied with the additional information provided?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Back at your first statement, Mr. Berikoff, at page 3, which is the same reference in B/C/S, you reference several locations in Knin which are military targets in your indication. And you assign letters to each of these on an aerial photograph which I believe you submitted along with the first statement; however, it is it not appended as a specific number itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I would like to bring that up, please, Madam Registrar. It's 65 ter 1830. My apologies to the Court for the light contrast between the background colours and the markings; however, I thought it was important to maintain the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Mr. Berikoff, is this the photograph to which you are referring in your first statement when you indicate place names with letters besides them?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you explain to the Court what the distinction is between the locations which are circled in pink and those in blue?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Those areas that are in blue indicate where either residential areas or where rounds had impacted. Those that are in pink are those areas that I considered likely military targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I noticed in your third statement - and we don't need to pull this up - but the reference is at page 8, line 27 to 36, where you reference the Knin general supply as a military target. So I would like - if I could have the assistance, please, of the usher - to have you mark in red the location of the Knin general supply, with the understanding that you've identified this as a military target.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: With that addition, Your Honour, I would move to admit the aerial photograph of Knin, 65 ter 1830.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P746, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P746, that is therefore 65 ter 1830, but additionally marked today by the witness. So, in addition to the markings already made, P746 is admitted into evidence. I'm just looking at this map, Mr. Russo. You apologised for not being there a lot of contrast. Is there any copy which would ensure that I'm not missing one of the earlier markings. I mean, the last one done in court is clear, but the other ones I'm a bit afraid that I might miss some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If it would please the Court, Your Honour, I would ask the witness to simply remark all of the ones here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes the work is done by the Defence. I don't know whether we could expect a similar thing. Mr. Kehoe, Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't have that directly, Your Honour, on this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see. On this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's in the spirit of not overloading Your Honour with military targets and stuff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I fully understand. I'm not blaming for you not having done the job which should have been done by the Prosecution. I don't think it is useful to ask the witness to do the job again. Perhaps there is a way of producing a copy which leaves me not in doubt whether I would miss any one; and then if you agree with the Prosecution that you didn't change anything, then I think it would assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That will be fine, Your Honour. I will have a computer-enhanced image uploaded for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And now if we could please move, Mr. Berikoff, to your third statement, which is D284. And at page 2, line 9, which, in the B/C/S translation, appears at page 2, lines 8 to 9, there you reference a document attached as "A".

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could now refer to 65 ter 2105.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, is the document now on the screen the document which is referred to as document "A" attached to your third statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you prepare this particular document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Again, can you tell the Court what the circumstances were of its preparation?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Once again, it was in conjunction with the award I was nominated for. As well, I was tasked to do an overall assessment of the activity in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. There are a few clarifications to this document that I'd like to take you through. Focussing on paragraph 1-B which discusses the mortar incident at the intersection, There you state: "When the HV troops entered Knin, there was strict restriction of movement (ROM); however, I was able to travel into Knin on a trip to the hospital. As we passed the previously bagged bodies, I noticed that the dead soldiers were removed from their bagged and that their bodies had been mutilated." Can you please clarify whether when you saw these soldiers out of the body-bags you were actually en route to a trip to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: That was in the late afternoon of the 5th of August. A Croat officer had come to the gate and indicated to us that there were a number of Serbs that wanted to come into the compound to be placed under UN protection. The Croat officer said that if we were to provide the drivers and the vehicle, they would provide the escort to ensure that we were able to get to the location where the Serbs were and bring them back to the compound. On our way out of the compound, and down the main road going into Knin before we got to the bridge, we were fired upon or over our heads by Croat soldiers an ordered to turn around. On the way back to the compound, myself and Captain Rob Williams saw, in fact, it wasn't two bodies, it was just the one soldier where his -- the body-bag was open. The soldier was out. The bag and everything was run over by a tank, and the bag and the body was riddled with bullet-holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And had that Croat officer who came to the gate told you that these Serbs who wanted refuge were at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I don't recall the -- the location of where they were. They were either at the hospital or they were at the middle school or school downtown.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move to paragraph 1-E which discusses your trip into Knin on 8 August and the looting and destruction that you witnessed on that date, including specifically damage done to General Forand's residence. And in that paragraph, you state: "Either HV troops or Croatian special police were likely responsible as they were all in the area." I'd like to you clarify, first, whether the damage you're attributing in Knin to HV or special police is the damage to Knin generally or just the damage to General Forand's residence?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I would say it is the damage done to Knin in general, not just to General Forand's place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you also clarify whether you witnessed special police - that is, the troops in grey uniforms - looting or committing acts of destruction in Knin itself.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: It was a combination of both.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally, moving to paragraph 1-H where you discuss your trip into Civljane on 11 August, and you state you "witnessed HV troops, including the special police, going into numerous residences." Again, I'd like you to clarify for the court whether you actually saw special police - that is, the individuals in grey uniforms - going into the residences in Civljane?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: In Civljane -- it was actually en route to Civljane. In Civljane itself, it was military and -- HV military personnel. They had also taken over the UN compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSS
utterances.text: With those clarifications, Your Honour, I would move to admit 65 ter 2105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P747, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P747 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Moving back to your third statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, again, we don't need to pull this up, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: But at page 3, you reference a document attached as document "D"?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: So, Madam Registrar, if we could have 65 ter 1177. And for the court's clarification, I'm not calling up B or C, because B was also attached to the previous statement and is already in evidence; C are a collection of the letters from Cermak regarding freedom of movement which are also in evidence; and the document which is being pulled up now is the journal. And I had indicated earlier that I didn't call up the previous journal which was attached to the first statement, and I will have the witness explain the distinction between the two journals for the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, can you tell the Court whether the document on the screen is the document referred to as "D" in your third statement.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you prepare this particular document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you could, please, explain to the Court the circumstances under which you created this particular journal.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: The journal was prepared -- a handwritten journal was prepared. When I first found out that I was being deployed to the former Yugoslavia, I started my own diary. The notes in my handwritten journal are basically notes throughout the day. I had made my entries daily based on the events of the day and when I had a bit of spare time to write. When I got to Sarajevo on or around the 6th of September, I started to transpose it into an electronic form. In doing so, I expanded on some of the areas based on my own recollection of the events that took place, and it was an ongoing project. It was notes for myself to be kept to myself. It was for no other reason, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And the journal that you handed to the ICTY investigator along with your first statement, can you tell Court how that relates to this particular journal?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Can you explain in what context, please, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Sure. Attached to your first statement is a journal which date-wise goes from the 30th of July until approximately the 15th of August. The journal which you've identified as document "D" attached to your third statement goes from 17 July to 6 September. If you can, please, tell the Court what is the difference is between the earlier shorter version and this version?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: As I indicate a few minutes ago, it was an ongoing project of mine, and I was expanding it as I was remembering things to put into my journal, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And comparing between the journal on the screen which is marked "D" to the earlier electronic version and to your handwritten statement, can you tell Court which of those three you consider to be the most complete and the most accurate version of events?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I would consider the latest one, the 17 July to 6 September, to be the more accurate of all of my journals, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move now for the admission of 65 ter 1177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P748, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P748 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, moving back to your third statement, Mr. Berikoff, beginning at page 61, line 5; and in the B/C/S translation, this appears at page 43, beginning at line 43. And in that portion of your third statement, Mr. Berikoff, you reference a number of photographs that you supplied to the ICTY investigator; I believe it is 154 photographs. And in the pages which follow, you identify 41 specific photographs by number and describe each one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could, Madam Registrar, please have 65 ter 5404?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: While that is it being pulled up, Mr. Berikoff, let me ask you: Did you have a chance to review an Index of photographs plus the photographs themselves to determine whether or not that Index plus the photographs accurately reflect the specific photographs that you identify and discuss in your third statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did. However, the photo -- the indexing was done to the best of my recollection. It's been 13 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And the document on the screen, is that the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could scroll in a few pages, or perhaps just one more page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at that document, Mr. Berikoff, is this the document that you reviewed and compared to your second statement --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: -- I'm sorry, your third statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: My third statement, yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And does this document accurately reflect the photographs which you reference in your third statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move for the admission of 65 ter 5404.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P749, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P749 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honour, I would just like to move through this very quickly. Of the 154 photographs provided by Mr. Berikoff along with his third statement, I've taken the liberty of categorising only a selection of those photographs into four separate categories. I have sent some notification of this to the Defence, and I would like to submit each category of photographs as a separate exhibit. I thought that might assist the Court. And if we could have, then, 65 ter 5399. And for the Court's information, this is a collection of photographs which indicate that they are photographs of shelling damage in residential areas of Knin, and I would move for the admission of 65 ter 5399. And I would also advise the Court that between the categories, there is some overlap between the previous collection of photographs, but I thought it would be easier reference for the Court to decide by category what it chose to review.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear no objections. Madam Registrar, 65 ter 5399 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be Exhibit P750, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P750 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to save a bit of time, rather than calling up all of the collections, 65 ter 5400 is a collection of photographs representing and identified by the witness as photographs of acts of burning or destruction within Knin itself; 65 ter 5401 is a collection of photographs depicting burning and acts of destruction outside of Knin; and 65 ter 5402 are a few photographs of Cetina valley which I thought the Court might appreciate getting at look at. So, if there is no quarrel, I would move for the admission of 5400, 5401, and 5402.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Just a question: Are these all of these included in 5404?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: They are not all included in 5404, but they are included in the 154, which Mr. Berikoff gave to the investigator, along with his third statement. MR. KUZMANOVIC. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that the total, then, will be more than 41?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections, no quarrels. Madam Registrar, 65 ter 5400 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be Exhibit P751, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P751 is admitted into evidence. P5401?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be Exhibit P752.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is admitted into evidence. P5402?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be Exhibit P753, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is admitted into evidence. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Berikoff, if we could now move to your fourth and final statement, which is P741, and moving to page 3 of that exhibit. And by the way, that is tab 4 in your binder. P741 at page 3, paragraph 7, which is the same citation in the B/C/S translation, you reference a video which was taken by an individual named Garth Pritchard. And I would like you to please to explain to the Court the circumstances of how that video was taken.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Garth Pritchard was a journalist for one of the television companies in Canada. He had come to take a video of, I guess, the combination of the Canadian soldiers up in the Benkovac-Rastovic area; as well, he made a trip down to our area in Knin. I was tasked by either General Leslie or General Forand to take him around to the area. Myself and Master Bombardier Parlee were his escorts, and we took him to various locations throughout the sector where he televised various areas of destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we have portions of this video identified by the witness that - I don't want to play them for the Court - I would just like to submit them on the basis of the supplemental statement and the information provided by Mr. Berikoff. So I would move for the admission of - and, again, we don't need to call them up - 65 ter 5405, this is this video at counter references 6 minutes 54 to 14 minutes 35; 65 ter 5406, our counter reference is 2425 to 3321; and 65 ter 5407, our counter reference is 3405 and 3802 [Realtime transcript read in error "3402". I would simply move for the admission of all three of those portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, could you please check whether what we have on the transcript at this moment whether that is it correct, because giving numbers in a quick sequence is at risk of being mis-transcribed, not because of lack of competence of the transcriber but because of speed of speech of the person who presents it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is only one correction to be made, and that is with respect to 65 ter 5407; and in that instance, the counter reference is actually 3405 to 3802.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Do I, then, understand that you only want these portions to be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and we will be submitting those portions and the translations for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections, as far as I am aware of at this moment. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 05405 will be Exhibit P754, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P754 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 05406 will be Exhibit P755.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P755 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And 65 ter 05407 will be Exhibit P756, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P756 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Russo, if you would allow me just to go back to the selection of photographs theme-oriented, so to say. It is my recollection that the witness statements contain an observation that not for all of the 154 photographs, he has time and place available. Now, we have seen this selection of 41, where there is an indication on this spreadsheet of time and place. Now, you have made another selection, of course, which the Chamber was not able to immediately verify and check. Now, for all those photographs which appear in these series - damage in Knin, damage outside Knin, damage in the Cetina valley - are these photographs of which time and place are always known and documented.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: To be clear, Your Honour, the photographs which are specifically referenced in the third statement and which are described do not contain information regarding the date and the time that the photograph was taken. That kind of specific information is not available for those photographs. Likewise, with the additional photographs which, as you indicate correctly, are organised by theme. We have only general time-frame for those photographs and I can ask the witness do discuss that, but we could not have specific dates and times for those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just asking because it might -- of course, the probative value of the photographs might be influenced by lack of certain information. But since there was no objections, the series are admitted into evidence, but just for the Chamber's information. Then please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Back to your fourth statement, Mr. Berikoff, and this time at paragraph 8, you reference another video which was taken by Mr. Pritchard. Are the circumstances of that video similar to the ones to the video we just discussed?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I would simply like to admit a portion of this video, not show it to the Court, and that would be 65 ter 5408, the counter reference for which is 02422.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P757, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P757 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And we -- if we could move now to also in your fourth statement, this time at paragraph 6, and you reference two maps which you provided to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The first map, if I could have 65 ter 5393.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Locking at this map, Mr. Berikoff, can you tell the Court whether this is the map which you reference in your fourth statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: This is one of the maps, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if I could move for the admission of 5393, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there are no objections, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P758, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P758 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could now have 65 ter 5392.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Berikoff, is the map on the screen the map you reference in your fourth statement as "PB-2"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is the northern portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I would move now for the admission of 65 ter 5392.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P759, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Russo, the description on your list is both in both -- no, I see, no. No. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now please have document 65 ter 2995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, are you familiar with this particular document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the document, yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court the -- first of all, did you prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court, if you know, how it was prepared or who prepared it?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: A presentation was given to personnel in Knin and Sector South headquarters. I'm not sure who prepared it; but based on the text of the -- of the document itself, it may have been Colonel Tymchuk or General Leslie.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And are you familiar enough with the contents of this document to indicate or explain to the Court whether you believe the information contained in it to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the contents; but to say that it is accurate or not would, you have to ask the originator of the document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court what exactly your involvement was with this particular document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: The only involvement I had with this document was to forward it on to General Leslie, or Colonel Leslie at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And why was it that you forwarded it on to General Leslie?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I was requested by Leslie.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on the fact that the witness simply indicates that this document was apparently drafted by someone within the HQ compound, was the subject of a presentation, and was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. That is not what he said. That is not what he said. He doesn't know where the origination of the document comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think he indicated that he doesn't know who drafted the document, but that it was the subject of a protection, it was requested to be sent -- requested from General Leslie to be sent from UNCRO Sector South --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's check. Looking at page 44, line 1, let's first seek clarification from the witness because there are two different interpretations of that line. Mr. Russo, you have heard what Mr. Kehoe says is not in the testimony, and you apparently take a different interpretation. Let's ask the witness what the link was between the presentation and the preparation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, you've already indicated that you don't know exactly who drafted it. Do you know who gave this presentation?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: No, I do not. I was not in attendance at the presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: How do you know it was a presentation?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF
utterances.text: I had heard, and it is only hearsay, that there was going to be a presentation to various people in the headquarters.
